frase_gancho.texto: A wall of serpents that devour flayed figures, swallowing them at the waist.

puente_narrativo.texto: We remain in Tula with a wall of serpents: the relief that marked the boundary of the main temple area.

guion_corto.texto: Coatepantli means wall of serpents. It comes from two Nahuatl words, cóatl, serpent, and pantli, wall. This slab belongs to the Wall of Serpents of Tula, on the rear face of Pyramid B. It was a sacred ornamental wall that marked the boundary of the main temple area. It is Toltec, from the Early Postclassic period. The basalt is carved in low relief with incised lines, and it was originally painted red, blue, and white. In the central band, rattlesnakes with undulating bodies hold and devour, by the middle, skeletons or flayed human figures. The Mexica took it as a model. They built an identical wall of serpents around the Sacred Precinct of Tenochtitlan.

guion_largo.texto:
A wall made of serpents. That is what Coatepantli means, from the Nahuatl cóatl, serpent, and pantli, wall.

The Wall of Serpents is in Tula, on the rear face of Pyramid B, also called the Temple of Tlahuizcalpantecuhtli. It is a Toltec work from the Early Postclassic. It was a sacred ornamental wall that marked the boundary of the main temple area.

This slab is made of basalt, carved in low relief with incised lines. It was originally polychrome, in red, blue, and white. The upper and lower cornices were decorated with crenellations and geometric stepped-fret patterns.

In the central band runs a continuous frieze. Rattlesnakes, with undulating bodies, hold and devour, by the middle, skeletons or flayed human figures.

The scene is interpreted as symbolizing the transformation of flesh and human sacrifice. It also stands for the rebirth of the soul and of the sun. It is a harsh image, and at the same time it speaks of cycles: what dies is transformed.

The Wall of Serpents served as a model for the Mexica. They raised an identical wall of serpents around the Sacred Precinct of Tenochtitlan and another in Tenayuca.

Look closely at the bodies of the serpents. The interlocking designs imitate the rattle, and their repeated rhythm gives the idea of a living wall.

texto: Look for the undulating bodies of the rattlesnakes.
Find the flayed figure they hold in their jaws.
Look at the crenellations and stepped-fret patterns on the cornices.

texto.Material: Basalt carved in low relief and incision, originally polychrome
texto.Origin: Tula, Hidalgo (Wall of Serpents, rear face of Pyramid B)
texto.Dimensions: Individual slab: 32.3 cm high x 105 cm wide x 5.5 cm thick

texto.pregunta: Myth: The Coatepantli was a defensive wall to protect Tula from enemies.
texto.respuesta: Reality: It was a sacred ornamental wall that marked the boundary of the main temple area. Its frieze speaks of sacrifice and rebirth.
